facebook.content_angle: Stroke rate vs stroke length trade-off — how most competitive swimmers chase cadence and sacrifice the distance-per-stroke efficiency that actually determines race pace
facebook.post_text:
Faster turnover doesn't always mean a faster time. ⚡

Most swimmers hit a plateau and instinctively spin their arms faster — but higher stroke rate without the distance to back it up just means working harder to go the same speed.

Here's what the data shows:
👉 Elite 100m freestyle swimmers average 1.8–2.1 metres per stroke — most club swimmers manage 1.2–1.4
👉 Closing that gap by just 0.4 metres per stroke removes 4–6 strokes from a 100m race
👉 Fewer strokes at the same pace means less energy burned and more speed held in the final 25m

The fastest swimmers aren't always the ones turning over quickest — they're the ones getting the most out of every single pull. 🔥

✔️ Drill focus: count your strokes per lap and aim to reduce by two without slowing your tempo
✔️ Use a tempo trainer to hold rate constant while you build stroke length
✔️ Film yourself from above — a dropped elbow kills DPS before your pull even loads
